decks.domain: Right of way, signals and signs

cards.front: Complete the guidance about right of way and processions, beginning with “Right-of-way rules guide yielding and the order of entry,”.
cards.back: Right-of-way rules guide yielding and the order of entry, but drivers must consider the actual situation rather than assume priority automatically.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about right of way and processions, beginning with “Yield to a driver already at”.
cards.back: Yield to a driver already at the intersection or arriving there before you.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about right of way and processions, beginning with “When turning left, yield to”.
cards.back: When turning left, yield to traffic approaching in the opposite lane.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about right of way and processions, beginning with “At an all-way stop, drivers who arrive simultaneously”.
cards.back: At an all-way stop, drivers who arrive simultaneously must yield to the driver on the right.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about right of way and processions, beginning with “When entering a public highway from a”.
cards.back: When entering a public highway from a driveway or private road, yield to highway traffic.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about right of way and processions, beginning with “A driver on an entrance or acceleration ramp must”.
cards.back: A driver on an entrance or acceleration ramp must yield to vehicles already on the limited-access or interstate highway.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about right of way and processions, beginning with “Yield to pedestrians, bicyclists and”.
cards.back: Yield to pedestrians, bicyclists and drivers still within the intersection.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about right of way and processions, beginning with “The funeral-procession rule says only its first”.
cards.back: The funeral-procession rule says only its first vehicle must obey traffic signs and signals.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about right of way and processions, beginning with “Vehicles in a funeral procession must use their headlights,”.
cards.back: Vehicles in a funeral procession must use their headlights, and other drivers must not cut into or interfere with the procession.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about right of way and processions, beginning with “Traffic-control devices include signals, signs, road markings and”.
cards.back: Traffic-control devices include signals, signs, road markings and directions from police, highway workers and school crossing guards.

decks.domain: Right of way, signals and signs

cards.front: Complete the guidance about pedestrian hybrid beacons, beginning with “A pedestrian hybrid beacon helps people cross busy”.
cards.back: A pedestrian hybrid beacon helps people cross busy or faster roads at midblock crossings and uncontrolled intersections.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about pedestrian hybrid beacons, beginning with “The pedestrian hybrid beacon described in the handbook”.
cards.back: The pedestrian hybrid beacon described in the handbook has two red lenses above one yellow lens.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about pedestrian hybrid beacons, beginning with “A pedestrian hybrid beacon stays dark”.
cards.back: A pedestrian hybrid beacon stays dark until a pedestrian presses the call button.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about pedestrian hybrid beacons, beginning with “After activation, the beacon follows a yellow-to-red sequence with”.
cards.back: After activation, the beacon follows a yellow-to-red sequence with steady and flashing lights directing motorists to slow and stop.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about pedestrian hybrid beacons, beginning with “The handbook says the pedestrian display then flashes WALK”.
cards.back: The handbook says the pedestrian display then flashes WALK and the beacon returns dark after the pedestrian crosses safely.

decks.domain: Right of way, signals and signs

cards.front: Complete the guidance about traffic signals, beginning with “Vertical traffic signals normally show red above yellow above”.
cards.back: Vertical traffic signals normally show red above yellow above green, while horizontal signals place red left, yellow center and green right.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about traffic signals, beginning with “A steady red signal requires a complete stop and”.
cards.back: A steady red signal requires a complete stop and waiting for green and clear crossing traffic before proceeding straight.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about traffic signals, beginning with “A right turn on red is allowed only after”.
cards.back: A right turn on red is allowed only after stopping completely when safe and when no sign forbids the turn.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about traffic signals, beginning with “Before turning on red, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists and”.
cards.back: Before turning on red, yield to pedestrians, bicyclists and vehicles, then turn safely while remaining in the proper lane.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about traffic signals, beginning with “A flashing red light is treated like a”.
cards.back: A flashing red light is treated like a stop sign: stop fully, then continue only when safe.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about traffic signals, beginning with “A red arrow prohibits movement in its direction until”.
cards.back: A red arrow prohibits movement in its direction until it goes out and a green arrow or green light appears.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about traffic signals, beginning with “A steady yellow light warns that red is”.
cards.back: A steady yellow light warns that red is next and requires stopping when stopping is safe.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about traffic signals, beginning with “If yellow appears after the vehicle is already”.
cards.back: If yellow appears after the vehicle is already in the intersection, continue through instead of stopping there.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about traffic signals, beginning with “A flashing yellow signal calls”.
cards.back: A flashing yellow signal calls for reduced speed and caution.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about traffic signals, beginning with “A yellow arrow means protected turning is ending, so”.
cards.back: A yellow arrow means protected turning is ending, so prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic before turning.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about traffic signals, beginning with “A flashing yellow left arrow permits a cautious left”.
cards.back: A flashing yellow left arrow permits a cautious left turn only when safe after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about traffic signals, beginning with “Oncoming traffic has a green signal while”.
cards.back: Oncoming traffic has a green signal while the described flashing-yellow left arrow is displayed.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about traffic signals, beginning with “A steady green permits proceeding but does not remove”.
cards.back: A steady green permits proceeding but does not remove duties to yield to emergency vehicles and others required by law.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about traffic signals, beginning with “When a stopped driver receives green, crossing”.
cards.back: When a stopped driver receives green, crossing traffic must clear before the driver enters.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about traffic signals, beginning with “A left turn on a steady green is allowed”.
cards.back: A left turn on a steady green is allowed only when safe, with oncoming traffic having priority and any left-turn prohibition still obeyed.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about traffic signals, beginning with “During a right or left turn, watch”.
cards.back: During a right or left turn, watch for pedestrians crossing in front of the vehicle.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about traffic signals, beginning with “A green arrow permits turning in its indicated direction,”.
cards.back: A green arrow permits turning in its indicated direction, with no oncoming or crossing traffic expected during that arrow.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about traffic signals, beginning with “When a signal malfunctions, a driver facing”.
cards.back: When a signal malfunctions, a driver facing green may proceed cautiously under SDCL thirty-two-twenty-eight-two.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about traffic signals, beginning with “When a signal malfunctions, a driver facing”.
cards.back: When a signal malfunctions, a driver facing yellow may proceed cautiously under SDCL thirty-two-twenty-eight-three.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about traffic signals, beginning with “A red or completely dark malfunctioning signal”.
cards.back: A red or completely dark malfunctioning signal must be treated as a stop sign.

decks.domain: Right of way, signals and signs

cards.front: Complete the guidance about warning signs and crossbucks, beginning with “A sign’s shape, color, symbols and wording help identify”.
cards.back: A sign’s shape, color, symbols and wording help identify whether it communicates rules, hazards, directions, locations or services.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about warning signs and crossbucks, beginning with “Warning signs usually have a diamond shape with”.
cards.back: Warning signs usually have a diamond shape with a yellow background and black words or symbols.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about warning signs and crossbucks, beginning with “Some school-zone, school-crossing and”.
cards.back: Some school-zone, school-crossing and pedestrian-crossing warnings use fluorescent yellow.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about warning signs and crossbucks, beginning with “A warning sign announces possible danger or a special”.
cards.back: A warning sign announces possible danger or a special road situation and may require slowing or preparing to stop.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about warning signs and crossbucks, beginning with “Before a rail crossing, a round yellow sign with”.
cards.back: Before a rail crossing, a round yellow sign with an X and black RR letters warns drivers to slow, look, listen and prepare to stop for an approaching train.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about warning signs and crossbucks, beginning with “A white X-shaped crossbuck marked Railroad”.
cards.back: A white X-shaped crossbuck marked Railroad Crossing stands at the highway-rail intersection.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about warning signs and crossbucks, beginning with “At a crossbuck crossing, an approaching train or rail vehicle requires stopping”.
cards.back: At a crossbuck crossing, an approaching train or rail vehicle requires stopping behind the stop line or before the intersection is clear.

decks.domain: Right of way, signals and signs

cards.front: Complete the guidance about rail-crossing warnings, beginning with “A multiple-track sign warns that another”.
cards.back: A multiple-track sign warns that another track and another train may be present.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about rail-crossing warnings, beginning with “Always check for additional tracks and trains because some”.
cards.back: Always check for additional tracks and trains because some multiple-track crossings lack the number-of-tracks sign and some crossings have no lights.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about rail-crossing warnings, beginning with “Alternately flashing rail-crossing”.
cards.back: Alternately flashing rail-crossing lights require a stop.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about rail-crossing warnings, beginning with “Never drive around”.
cards.back: Never drive around a lowered rail-crossing gate.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about rail-crossing warnings, beginning with “Where a rail-crossing bell or horn sounds,”.
cards.back: Where a rail-crossing bell or horn sounds, do not cross until the warning sound stops.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about rail-crossing warnings, beginning with “The railroad emergency-notification sign provides a dispatch phone”.
cards.back: The railroad emergency-notification sign provides a dispatch phone number for reporting crossing, track or train problems.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about rail-crossing warnings, beginning with “The emergency-notification number is generally on a”.
cards.back: The emergency-notification number is generally on a blue sign at or near the crossing.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about rail-crossing warnings, beginning with “The same sign’s DOT number identifies the”.
cards.back: The same sign’s DOT number identifies the crossing location for emergency crews and railroad staff.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about rail-crossing warnings, beginning with “Give the crossing’s DOT identifier when reporting trouble so”.
cards.back: Give the crossing’s DOT identifier when reporting trouble so dispatch can identify it and warn or slow approaching trains.

decks.domain: Right of way, signals and signs

cards.front: Complete the guidance about work-zone controls, beginning with “Work-zone signs are generally orange with black”.
cards.back: Work-zone signs are generally orange with black markings and have diamond or rectangular shapes.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about work-zone controls, beginning with “Work-zone warnings may announce workers, lower speeds,”.
cards.back: Work-zone warnings may announce workers, lower speeds, detours, slow equipment or changing road surfaces.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about work-zone controls, beginning with “Obey a work-zone controller’s signs or”.
cards.back: Obey a work-zone controller’s signs or flags directing travel, slowing or stopping.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about work-zone controls, beginning with “Work-zone drums, cones, panels and barricades guide”.
cards.back: Work-zone drums, cones, panels and barricades guide traffic away from hazardous or closed areas.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about work-zone controls, beginning with “Temporary work-zone signals may be used, and a driver”.
cards.back: Temporary work-zone signals may be used, and a driver stopping there must stop at a white line when one is present.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about work-zone controls, beginning with “In a work zone, slow down, expect”.
cards.back: In a work zone, slow down, expect sudden stops and avoid following too closely.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about work-zone controls, beginning with “Speeding fines in a”.
cards.back: Speeding fines in a work zone may be doubled.

decks.domain: Right of way, signals and signs

cards.front: Complete the guidance about regulatory signs, beginning with “Regulatory signs communicate laws for direction, lanes, turns,”.
cards.back: Regulatory signs communicate laws for direction, lanes, turns, speed, parking and other situations that drivers must obey.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about regulatory signs, beginning with “Regulatory signs are white with black, red or green”.
cards.back: Regulatory signs are white with black, red or green markings and may be square, rectangular or specially shaped.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about regulatory signs, beginning with “A red circle and slash over”.
cards.back: A red circle and slash over a regulatory symbol prohibit the action represented.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about regulatory signs, beginning with “Black-and-white speed signs state the maximum”.
cards.back: Black-and-white speed signs state the maximum permitted speed or a required minimum.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about regulatory signs, beginning with “Use the posted maximum only in ideal conditions and”.
cards.back: Use the posted maximum only in ideal conditions and reduce speed for slippery roads, precipitation, ice or limited visibility.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about regulatory signs, beginning with “On a road with a minimum speed, use another”.
cards.back: On a road with a minimum speed, use another road if that posted minimum is too fast for you.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about regulatory signs, beginning with “A stop sign is red with”.
cards.back: A stop sign is red with white lettering and has eight sides.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about regulatory signs, beginning with “At a stop sign, stop behind an existing stop”.
cards.back: At a stop sign, stop behind an existing stop line or crosswalk, or before the sign when neither is present, then check every direction and yield.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about regulatory signs, beginning with “A yield sign is a”.
cards.back: A yield sign is a downward-pointing red-and-white triangle with red lettering.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about regulatory signs, beginning with “A yield sign requires slowing and giving priority”.
cards.back: A yield sign requires slowing and giving priority to traffic in the intersection or road being entered.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about regulatory signs, beginning with “On a one-way street, travel only in the”.
cards.back: On a one-way street, travel only in the arrow’s direction and never turn or drive against it.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about regulatory signs, beginning with “No-passing signs and pavement markings identify passing-zone beginnings”.
cards.back: No-passing signs and pavement markings identify passing-zone beginnings and endings and places where passing is prohibited.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about regulatory signs, beginning with “Passing-zone placement considers visible distance and hidden”.
cards.back: Passing-zone placement considers visible distance and hidden hazards such as hills, curves, intersections and driveways.

cards.front: Complete the guidance about regulatory signs, beginning with “Even where passing is permitted, pass only when”.
cards.back: Even where passing is permitted, pass only when safe in the actual road and traffic conditions.
